question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }(1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use ${sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }(1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$
